question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can factor out a $(-5)$ from each of the terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}100+40y-5{y}^{2} & =-5({y}^{2}-8y-20) & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to factor the polynomial ${y}^{2}-8y-20$ in parentheses.

We start by listing the factor pairs of the constant term $(-20).$ The constant term is negative, so that means one of the factors is negative and the other is positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \times (-20) \\ (-1) & \times 20 \\ 2 & \times (-10) \\ (-2) & \times 10 \\ 4 & \times (-5) \\ (-4) & \times 5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $(-8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+(-20) & =-19 & \times  \\ -1+20 & =19 & \times  \\ 2+(-10) & =-8 & ✓ \\ -2+10 & =8 & \times  \\ 4+(-5) & =-1 & \times  \\ -4+5 & =1 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

Using the factor pair identified above, we write the linear term as $-8y=2y-10y$ and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5({y}^{2}-8y-20) & = \\ -5({y}^{2}+2y-10y-20) & = \\ -5(({y}^{2}+2y)+(-10y-20)) & = \\ -5(y(y+2)-10(y+2)) & = \\ -5(y-10)(y+2) & \end{aligned}
$$
